subject: Clarify billing: rolling session windows, KV cache credits, and pilot discount
messages:
From: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@atlashealth.com>

Subject: Billing: short-session traffic and longer context runs (pilot pricing ask)

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. A few questions came up while we mapped our usage to your pricing model. We attached a small sample of typical traffic (atlas_usage_sample.csv) and the billing Q&A PDF you sent earlier for reference.

High-level ask: we want to understand how token accounting and rounding interact for two common patterns in our workload:

- A: high-frequency short messages from users (150 - 400 tokens each) sent in bursts (3–8 requests) over 30–90 seconds (think chat).
- B: longer context inference where we send a ~8k-token document and request a 256-token summary (background batch jobs).

Specific clarifications we need before the pilot:
1) Do you round every individual request up to a per-request minimum? If so, is there any way to get short bursts aggregated so we don't pay a full minimum for each tiny reply?
2) How is the KV/prefix cache treated across these requests — will reusing the same conversation context reduce billed tokens?
3) For long-context jobs, are there any separate rounding or chunking rules (e.g., per-1k token chunk rounding) and how does that interact with summary generation costs?
4) We are also negotiating a 3-month pilot — would Redwood entertain a pilot concession that offsets the startup noise (spikes) while we stabilize usage?

Appreciate a clear, concise mapping we can include in our procurement pack.

Regards,
Emily Nguyen
Director of Product, Atlas Health

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Nguyen <emily.nguyen@atlashealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>

Subject: Re: Billing: short-session traffic and longer context runs (pilot pricing ask)

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear write-up and the sample. I looked through atlas_usage_sample.csv; excellent signal. I’ll summarize how our metering applies to each pattern and then propose a pilot concession we can offer.

Short answers up front:
- We bill on tokens consumed (input prompt tokens + output tokens) as reported by our tokenizer.
- We do have a session aggregation window that can reduce the effective minimums for short bursty traffic — details below.
- KV/prefix caching reduces repeated encoding work, but billed tokens still count any newly submitted tokens; we credit cross-request reuse in a predictable way.

Detailed breakdown:
1) Rolling session window and per-request minimums:
   - By default, each API call is metered and rounded up to the smaller of: (a) the per-request minimum floor of 100 tokens, or (b) the actual token count if >=100.
   - However, for interactive/chat-like traffic we support a 60-second rolling session window: multiple requests from the same session id within 60s are aggregated and billed as a single window. Aggregation sums the raw tokens then applies a single rounding floor of 50 tokens per window (instead of 100 per request). That is designed for bursty UX where users send several quick taps.
   - Implementation note: the session id is settable in the request header (x-rdw-session-id). If you don't set it we will attempt a heuristic grouping based on client IP + conversation metadata but that is less reliable for mobile clients.

2) KV/prefix cache behavior and credits:
   - Our runtime keeps a per-model KV cache for recent prefixes in the serving tier. When the same prefix is reused across requests, the runtime avoids re-encoding that prefix, which reduces latency and GPU work.
   - Billing is token-based, so if you re-send the full prompt text every request you'll generally be billed for those input tokens. To capture savings we recommend sending a short reference token/header (a stored-context id) instead of the full prompt for repeated context; requests using stored context reference only bill for the deltas (new tokens) plus a small storage-ref overhead (~5 tokens equivalent).
   - For closed pilots we can pre-populate shared contexts on the Dedicated pool and apply a small per-window cache-credit that effectively reduces billed tokens for repeated prefixes by a negotiated percentage.

3) Long-context batch jobs (8k doc + 256-token summary):
   - We meter the full number of tokens processed. For very long contexts we chunk internally for memory; however billing sums the logical tokens (end-to-end) and applies a chunk rounding policy of 200-token increments for contexts >4k tokens. So an 8k input will be charged at the full 8k (not rounded down), but internal chunking may mean the effective rounding is on 200-token boundaries for very high volumes — this is mostly to simplify GPU scheduling and only affects invoicing when you have many >4k requests.
   - Output tokens are billed normally and aggregated with the input for the request.

4) Pilot concession proposal (3 months):
   - For a limited 3-month pilot we can offer: (A) a 10% gross usage credit applied monthly to help with early spikes; (B) a session-aggregation default set to 120s for your pilot to help mobile UX; and (C) a one-time KV-cache pilot credit that reduces billed tokens for repeated prefixes by 15% for the pilot months.
   - To get to 25% you'd need a committed usage agreement (Reserved / Dedicated) — we can map commitment tiers if you want to discuss a post-pilot transition.

Next steps: I can loop in Contracts for a short addendum to the trial PO that captures the pilot credit terms above. Lauren, can you confirm whether the 10% credit should flow as a monthly invoice credit or a one-time pre-paid credit on the account?

If that all looks good Emily, I’ll prepare a short “metering map” we can attach to procurement to make costs predictable.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Jonas — quick operational note from legal/procurement side:

- If we set session-aggregation at 120s for the pilot, we should include explicit language that aggregation is pilot-only and will revert to 60s unless a post-pilot SLA change is agreed. Put this in the addendum.
- For the KV-cache "credit" we must define the metric ("15% reduction on billed input tokens attributable to stored-context references") and a way to audit it. Recommend we provide an automated report weekly and a one-time calculation at the end of the month for the credit applied.
- On invoice flow: Aditya, ops prefers the pilot 10% as a monthly invoice credit rather than prepayment; this keeps bookkeeping simpler for both sides.

Jonas — I can draft the short addendum (2–3 paragraphs) once you confirm the exact session window and whether we are exposing session id guidance in the doc.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference

Note: internal counsel prefers not to tie credits to uptime SLAs for pilot; credits should be usage-driven only.

Pilot terms (confirmed):
- Duration: 3 months starting on first production API call.
- Credits: 10% monthly invoice credit on gross metered usage.
- Session aggregation: pilot window = 120s (must pass x-rdw-session-id for reliable aggregation; we will include a short SDK snippet).
- KV-cache pilot credit: 15% reduction applied to billed input tokens attributable to stored-context references (automated weekly report; final monthly reconciliation).

Operational notes:
- We will provide the metering map doc and an SDK snippet for setting x-rdw-session-id in the next 24 hours.
- Aditya, please create the weekly report template and a HubSpot note referencing RDW-DEAL-2025-0817.

Emily — if you’re okay with the items above I’ll ask Contracts to prepare the addendum and we can get the pilot turned on. If you need the 25% figure we discussed earlier, we can model that as an option if Atlas converts to a 12‑month committed Dedicated contract after the pilot.

Best,
Jonas
